docs.text: WhiskDB # WhiskDB is an in-memory relational database and WebAssembly application host written in C++23 for Linux x86_64 . It eliminates traditional network boundaries and object-relational impedance by co-locating relational state and sandboxed server-side functions ( Whisks ) in the same physical memory space. Inspired by DuckDB , SpacetimeDB , and Convex , WhiskDB combines sub-millisecond query execution with configurable write-ahead log (WAL) persistence, zero-copy binary wire framing, and a native C++ client SDK and CLI. Architecture at a Glance # WhiskDB unites client communication, transaction execution, in-memory relational state, and durable persistence into a unified engine: ┌───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐ │ Whisk CLI & C++ Client SDK │ │ whisk repl │ whisk sql │ whisk ping │ whisk logs │ └───────────────────────────────┬───────────────────────────────┘ │ TCP Binary Wire Protocol │ (4-byte framing, Opcode, CRC32) ┌───────────────────────────────▼───────────────────────────────┐ │ WhiskDB Server │ │ │ │ ┌───────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐ │ │ │ Asynchronous Network Engine │ │ │ │ (Standalone Asio Event Loop) │ │ │ └───────────────────────────┬───────────────────────────┘ │ │ │ Request Dispatch │ │ ┌───────────────────────────▼───────────────────────────┐ │ │ │ In-Memory SQL Engine │ │ │ │ SQLite3 Amalgamation + Statement Cache │ │ │ │ Value Codec (Int64, Double, Text, Blob) │ │ │ └───────────────────────────┬───────────────────────────┘ │ │ │ Transaction Savepoint / WAL │ │ ┌───────────────────────────▼───────────────────────────┐ │ │ │ Storage & Durability Engine │ │ │ │ WAL Manager (Strict, Group Commit, Relaxed, Ephemeral)│ │ │ │ Snapshot Manager (Atomic Zstandard Checkpoints) │ │ │ └───────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘ │ └───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘ Core Capabilities # Capability Specification Key Benefit Language & Standard Modern C++23 Zero-overhead abstractions, std::string_view , std::span , and monadic Result<T> In-Memory SQL SQLite3 Amalgamation Full ACID transactions with sub-millisecond in-memory query execution Statement Caching Hash-keyed Prepared Statements Bypasses query parsing on hot paths for repeated execution Configurable Durability 4 DurabilityMode Profiles Select between strict ( fdatasync ), group_commit (batched), relaxed , and memory_only Binary Wire Protocol Length-Prefixed Framing Compact 4-byte big-endian framing with opcodes and CRC32 payload verification Client Ecosystem whisk CLI & WhiskClient SDK Interactive REPL, formatted ASCII tables, and native C++ client library Quick Start Preview # Start the Server # Launch the database daemon with default options ( group_commit durability on 0.0.0.0:8080 ): ./build/debug/app/whiskdb Connect via the CLI # Start the interactive REPL to query and inspect the server: ./build/debug/app/whisk repl whisk > CREATE TABLE users ( id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY , name TEXT , balance REAL ); Query OK , 0 rows affected ( round trip 0 . 42 ms ) whisk > INSERT INTO users ( name , balance ) VALUES ( 'Alice' , 150 . 50 ), ( 'Bob' , 82 . 00 ); Query OK , 2 rows affected , last_insert_rowid = 2 ( round trip 0 . 38 ms ) whisk > SELECT * FROM users ; + ----+-------+---------+ | id | name | balance | + ----+-------+---------+ | 1 | Alice | 150 . 50 | | 2 | Bob | 82 . 00 | + ----+-------+---------+ 2 rows in set ( 0 . 35 ms ) Academic Information # docs.text: WhiskDB Developer Guide # The WhiskDB Developer Guide specifies the normative engineering standards, internal subsystem architecture, coding conventions, and collaboration workflow for all team members and automated agents contributing to WhiskDB. 1. External Libraries & Ecosystem # WhiskDB relies on focused, lightweight dependencies managed via vcpkg or CMake's FetchContent : Library Header / Component Purpose Integration Method Standalone Asio asio.hpp ( asio_headers ) Asynchronous non-blocking network I/O, event loops, TCP server and client socket handling vcpkg / CMake FetchContent SQLite3 Amalgamation sqlite3.h ( sqlite3_static ) In-memory relational storage engine, SQL parsing, B-tree indexes, and ACID savepoint management Bundled C static library toml++ toml++/toml.hpp ( toml_headers ) Header-only C++20/23 TOML configuration file parser for config.toml vcpkg / CMake FetchContent Wasmtime C API wasm.h , wasmtime.h Sandboxed WebAssembly runtime for server-side Whisk module execution (in progress) System / Vendor archive Zero Heavy Frameworks WhiskDB avoids heavy all-in-one frameworks. All network protocols use length-prefixed binary frames built on top of standalone Asio rather than HTTP or heavy WebSocket stacks. 2. Coding Standards & Conventions (C++23) # Namespace Rule # All engine code under src/ and include/ must reside inside namespace database . Never write using namespace std; in any header or translation unit. Naming Conventions # WhiskDB follows DuckDB-inspired naming conventions, partially verified via clang-tidy : Target Convention Example Notes Files snake_case wal_manager.cpp , sql_engine.hpp Match class concept name Types (Classes, Structs, Enums, Aliases) PascalCase WhiskClient , WalManager , DurabilityMode Concrete and unambiguous Functions & Methods PascalCase ExecuteQuery() , AppendRecord() , Recover() Verb-noun phrases Variables & Members snake_case page_size , write_mutex_ , is_active_ Private members use trailing underscore Loop Indices Meaningful names in nested loops row_idx , col_idx , frame_idx i is allowed only in single, flat loops Types & Memory Management # No Raw Allocation : Never invoke raw new , delete , or malloc . Use smart pointers for dynamic allocation. Ownership Semantics : Default to std::unique_ptr for exclusive resource ownership. Use std::shared_ptr only when multiple distinct subsystems require shared lifetime. Indices and Offsets : Use idx_t ( uint64_t ) instead of raw size_t for counts, offsets, and collection indices. Fixed-Width Integers : Use explicit types ( int8_t .. int64_t , uint8_t .. uint64_t ) instead of ambiguous standard types like int or long . Scoped Enums : Always declare enum class . Specify the underlying storage type (e.g., : uint8_t ) when the enum is serialized over the wire or to disk: cpp enum class Opcode : uint8_t { Ping = 0x01, SqlQuery = 0x02, WhiskPublish = 0x03, WhiskCall = 0x04 }; Constants : Replace magic numbers with named constexpr constants. Control Flow & Class Layout # Explicit Braces : Always use {} braces for if , else , for , and while statements, even for single-line bodies. Return Early : Guard clauses and early returns keep indentation shallow. Virtual Overrides : Omit the virtual keyword on overriding member functions; use override or final exclusively. Class Section Layout : Order class definitions consistently: ```cpp class ExampleManager { public: // 1. Constructors & public member variables ExampleManager(); ~ExampleManager(); public: // 2. Public member functions Result Initialize(); private: // 3. Private helper functions Result FlushBuffer(); private: // 4. Private member variables std::string path_; idx_t buffer_size_ = 0; }; ``` 3. Error Handling & Invariant Policy # WhiskDB enforces a strict distinction between operational errors and developer bugs: Operational Errors ( Result<T> & ErrorCode ) # Expected runtime failures—such as network disconnects, invalid SQL syntax, table constraint violations, or missing files—must return Result<T> or status codes. Do not throw exceptions for expected operational flow. Result < QueryResult > result = client . Query ( "SELECT * FROM invalid_table;" ); if ( ! result ) { LOG_WARN ( "Query failed: {}" , result . error (). Message ()); return result . error (); } Invariant Assertions ( D_ASSERT ) # Use D_ASSERT(condition) generously to verify internal assumptions and developer invariants. Every D_ASSERT must include an explanatory comment on the preceding line: // Ensure the payload does not exceed the maximum allowable wire frame size D_ASSERT ( payload_len <= Framing :: MAX_PAYLOAD_SIZE ); D_ASSERT checks are active in Debug builds and must never be triggered by external user input. Fatal Failures # Exceptions are reserved strictly for unrecoverable system failures, such as memory allocation exhaustion or unrecoverable disk corruption. 4. Internal Subsystem Architecture # WhiskDB is composed of four modular internal subsystems: ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐ │ whiskdb core │ ├─────────────────┬─────────────────┬─────────────────────────┤ │ Network Layer │ SQL Engine │ Storage & Durability │ ├─────────────────┼─────────────────┼─────────────────────────┤ │ - Framing │ - SQLite3 :mem: │ - WalManager │ │ - Protocol │ - Cache │ - PosixFile │ │ - Asio Server │ - ValueCodec │ - SnapshotManager │ │ - TcpClient │ - Savepoints │ - CRC32 Verifier │ └─────────────────┴─────────────────┴─────────────────────────┘ 1. Network Layer ( include/network/ , src/network/ ) # Framing ( Framing ) : All packets use a 4-byte big-endian length prefix. Frames larger than MAX_PAYLOAD_SIZE (64 MB) are rejected. Protocol ( Protocol , Request , Response ) : Requests include an Opcode (1 byte) followed by payload bytes. Responses include a status code ( ErrorCode , 2 bytes), execution duration in microseconds ( exec_us , 8 bytes), and response payload. Asio Server ( Server , TcpSession ) : Scalable, non-blocking asynchronous TCP server running on standalone Asio. Sessions maintain dedicated receive buffers to minimize allocations. 2. SQL Engine Layer ( include/sql/ , src/sql/ ) # Engine Core ( SqlEngine ) : Wraps an in-memory SQLite3 handle ( :memory: ). Statement Cache ( StatementCache ) : Prepared statement cache keyed by SQL text hash, eliminating parsing and compilation overhead on repetitive queries. Value Codec ( ValueCodec ) : High-speed binary serializer and deserializer for SQL data types ( ValueType : Null , Int64 , Double , Text , Blob ), facilitating zero-copy decoding across wire packets. Transaction Guard ( TransactionGuard ) : Manages nested SQLite SAVEPOINT transactions with automatic rollback on error. 3. Storage & Durability Layer ( include/storage/ , src/storage/ ) # Write-Ahead Log ( WalManager ) : Appends binary transaction records ( WalRecordType::SqlStatement ) protected by CRC32 checksums to ./data/db.wal . Durability Modes ( DurabilityMode ) : Configurable flush behavior ( Strict , GroupCommit , Relaxed , MemoryOnly ). File I/O ( PosixFile ) : RAII POSIX file descriptor wrapper managing open , pwrite , pread , and fdatasync . Snapshot Manager ( SnapshotManager ) : Serializes full database state to disk checkpoints ( snapshot.db ) and safely resets the WAL log upon reaching record limits. 4. Client SDK & CLI Layer ( include/client/ , src/client/ , app/ ) # WhiskClient ( WhiskClient ) : Native C++ client handling socket connection, handshake, query execution, and error unwrapping. Table Formatter ( FormatResultTable ) : ASCII box-drawing table renderer with automatic column width calculation and execution metrics. Interactive REPL ( app/whisk.cpp ) : Interactive terminal client with multi-line statement continuation ( SplitStatements ), dot command execution ( .help , .ping , .logs , .snapshot ), and ANSI color error highlighting. 5. Build & Test Macros # WhiskDB provides unified development macros orchestrated by scripts/macro.sh : Macro Description Output Artifacts cmake build-debug Configures and builds all targets with Debug symbols and -Wall -Wextra -Wpedantic build/debug/ cmake build-release Configures and builds all targets with full -O3 compiler optimizations build/release/ cmake run-tests Compiles Debug target and executes all test suites via CTest with verbose failure logging Full CTest report cmake run-tests <regex> Runs only test suites matching the specified regex pattern (e.g., cmake run-tests wal ) Filtered test results cmake bench Builds Release and runs standard persistence and throughput benchmarks Benchmark metrics cmake clean Removes all build directories ( build/debug/ , build/release/ ) Clean workspace 6. Git & Collaboration Workflow # Every contributor and agent must follow WhiskDB's mandatory 5-step development lifecycle: [GitHub Issue] ──> [Branch off dev] ──> [Code & Test] ──> [Commit & Push] ──> [Open Pull Request] 1. Check & Update GitHub Issues # Inspect the target issue before writing code: gh issue view <issue-number> . Post an acknowledgement comment stating that work has begun in the feature branch. 2. Dedicated Feature Branch off dev # Always branch from the latest dev branch: sh git checkout dev git pull origin dev git checkout -b feat/issue-<issue-number>-<slug> 3. Build & Test Verification # Ensure zero compiler warnings and 100% test pass rate: sh cmake build-debug cmake run-tests 4. Conventional Commits # Use conventional commit prefixes: - feat(scope): add feature description (Closes #N) - fix(scope): fix bug description (Closes #N) - docs(scope): update documentation - test(scope): add test coverage 5. Pull Request Submission # For engine and feature code, open the PR targeting dev : sh gh pr create --base dev --head feat/issue-<issue-number>-<slug> --title "feat(scope): ..." --body "..." Reference the resolved issue ( Closes #N ) in the PR description. Work is complete only after the PR is submitted. 6. Documentation Branching & Deployment ( gh-pages ) # Documentation updates ( docs/ , mkdocs.yml ) belong strictly to their dedicated branch ( gh-pages ) and are published directly using mkdocs gh-deploy : mkdocs build --strict # Verify build integrity locally mkdocs gh-deploy # Deploy directly to the gh-pages branch Do not target or merge documentation-only updates into the dev branch.

docs.text: WhiskDB Development & Architecture # This page outlines the architectural scope of WhiskDB, the durability and reliability model, external library dependencies, and current development milestone progress. 1. Project Scope & Objectives # WhiskDB is built around four primary engineering pillars: Sandboxed In-Engine Code Execution : Co-locating business logic with in-memory database state using sandboxed WebAssembly execution to eliminate database network hops. Zero-Copy In-Memory Relational Access : Leveraging SQLite3 in :memory: mode coupled with prepared statement caching and binary value encoders for sub-millisecond query execution. Flexible Durability & Crash Recovery : Providing a high-performance write-ahead log (WAL) engine with configurable durability guarantees, CRC32 record integrity, and atomic checkpointing. Persistent Binary Wire Protocol : Delivering low-latency client communication through length-prefixed binary framing, native C++ SDK bindings, and an interactive CLI shell. 2. Durability Modes & Latency Profiles # WhiskDB supports four distinct durability modes ( DurabilityMode ) configured via durability_mode in config.toml or passed via the --durability CLI option. This allows deployments to tailor the trade-off between write latency and crash resilience: Durability Mode Config Aliases Disk Flush Strategy Crash Guarantee Typical Latency Recommended Workload strict sync Synchronous fdatasync on every committed transaction Zero data loss on sudden power loss or OS crash ~1–5 ms (I/O bound) Financial ledgers, high-value transactional records group_commit (Default) batched In-memory WAL ring buffer flushed via batched fdatasync (e.g. periodic or batch threshold) Bounded data loss window (up to batch interval); zero loss on process crash ~50–150 µs High-throughput OLTP, default production setting relaxed async WAL records written to OS page cache ( write() ); background asynchronous flush Survives process crashes; OS crash may lose unwritten page cache ~5–15 µs Real-time gaming, telemetry, high-ingestion streams memory_only ephemeral WAL disabled entirely; pure :memory: execution Volatile; data is reset on process termination < 2 µs Unit tests, ephemeral benchmarks, CI test runs Checkpointing & Snapshotting # To keep WAL replay times fast during recovery, WhiskDB automatically checkpoints state when the number of accumulated mutations reaches checkpoint_wal_records (default: 100,000 ): Atomic Flush : The database engine writes a consistent snapshot ( snapshot.db ). Log Truncation : Once the snapshot is verified on disk, the WAL file ( db.wal ) is truncated back to zero. Crash Recovery : On startup, Engine::Open() inspects ./data , loads the newest valid snapshot, and replays any trailing WAL records up to the crash point. 3. docs.text: This page outlines the architectural scope of WhiskDB, the durability and reliability model, external library dependencies, and current development milestone progress.
docs.title: WhiskDB Development & Architecture

docs.text: WhiskDB is built around four primary engineering pillars: Sandboxed In-Engine Code Execution : Co-locating business logic with in-memory database state using sandboxed WebAssembly execution to eliminate database network hops. Zero-Copy In-Memory Relational Access : Leveraging SQLite3 in :memory: mode coupled with prepared statement caching and binary value encoders for sub-millisecond query execution. Flexible Durability & Crash Recovery : Providing a high-performance write-ahead log (WAL) engine with configurable durability guarantees, CRC32 record integrity, and atomic checkpointing. Persistent Binary Wire Protocol : Delivering low-latency client communication through length-prefixed binary framing, native C++ SDK bindings, and an interactive CLI shell.
docs.title: 1. Project Scope & Objectives

docs.text: WhiskDB supports four distinct durability modes ( DurabilityMode ) configured via durability_mode in config.toml or passed via the --durability CLI option. This allows deployments to tailor the trade-off between write latency and crash resilience: Durability Mode Config Aliases Disk Flush Strategy Crash Guarantee Typical Latency Recommended Workload strict sync Synchronous fdatasync on every committed transaction Zero data loss on sudden power loss or OS crash ~1–5 ms (I/O bound) Financial ledgers, high-value transactional records group_commit (Default) batched In-memory WAL ring buffer flushed via batched fdatasync (e.g. periodic or batch threshold) Bounded data loss window (up to batch interval); zero loss on process crash ~50–150 µs High-throughput OLTP, default production setting relaxed async WAL records written to OS page cache ( write() ); background asynchronous flush Survives process crashes; OS crash may lose unwritten page cache ~5–15 µs Real-time gaming, telemetry, high-ingestion streams memory_only ephemeral WAL disabled entirely; pure :memory: execution Volatile; data is reset on process termination < 2 µs Unit tests, ephemeral benchmarks, CI test runs
docs.title: 2. Durability Modes & Latency Profiles

docs.text: To keep WAL replay times fast during recovery, WhiskDB automatically checkpoints state when the number of accumulated mutations reaches checkpoint_wal_records (default: 100,000 ): Atomic Flush : The database engine writes a consistent snapshot ( snapshot.db ). Log Truncation : Once the snapshot is verified on disk, the WAL file ( db.wal ) is truncated back to zero. Crash Recovery : On startup, Engine::Open() inspects ./data , loads the newest valid snapshot, and replays any trailing WAL records up to the crash point.

docs.text: WhiskDB User Guide # This guide covers running the WhiskDB server daemon, using the interactive whisk command-line interface (CLI), and integrating WhiskDB into applications using the native C++ Client SDK. 1. WhiskDB Server ( whiskdb ) # The whiskdb binary starts the persistent database server daemon. It initializes the storage engine, opens or recovers the database from disk snapshots and WAL logs, and accepts client TCP connections. Command-Line Usage # whiskdb [ --config <path> ] [ --data-dir <dir> ] [ --host <ip> ] [ --port <n> ] [ --durability <mode> ] Option Type Default Description --config <path> string ./config.toml Path to the TOML configuration file --data-dir <dir> string ./data Directory where WAL files and snapshot checkpoints are stored --host <ip> string 0.0.0.0 Network interface to bind for incoming client TCP connections --port <n> integer 8080 TCP port number to listen on ( 1 – 65535 ) --durability <mode> string group_commit Durability mode: strict , group_commit , relaxed , or memory_only -h , --help flag — Display usage instructions and exit Command-line flags override the corresponding values in config.toml . Configuration File ( config.toml ) # WhiskDB reads server settings from a TOML configuration file on startup: [config] data_directory = "./data" page_size = 4096 ipv4 = "0.0.0.0" port = 8080 # Durability profile: strict | group_commit | relaxed | memory_only durability_mode = "group_commit" # Automatic snapshot threshold: snapshot + reset WAL after N records (0 = disable) checkpoint_wal_records = 100000 Key Type Default Description data_directory string ./data Target directory for persistence artifacts ( db.wal , snapshot.db ) page_size integer 4096 Allocation block size in bytes ipv4 / host string 0.0.0.0 Listening IPv4 interface port integer 8080 Listening TCP port durability_mode string group_commit Durability mode balancing latency and crash safety checkpoint_wal_records integer 100000 Number of WAL mutations before triggering an automatic checkpoint 2. Whisk CLI Reference ( whisk ) # The whisk CLI provides an interactive database shell (REPL), health inspection, log streaming, and command-driven SQL execution over the persistent TCP protocol. Synopsis # whisk [ --host <ip> ] [ --port <n> ] <command> [ args ] Global Options # Option Default Description --host <ip> , --host=<ip> 127.0.0.1 WhiskDB server hostname or IP address --port <n> , --port=<n> 8080 WhiskDB server TCP port -h , --help — Display CLI usage information and exit Commands # Command Arguments Description repl (none) Start the interactive SQL shell with multi-line input and dot commands (default) ping (none) Ping the server and display measured round-trip latency in microseconds sql "<query>" Execute one or more SQL statements and render formatted result tables logs (none) Retrieve and display recent structured server-side engine logs snapshot (none) Trigger an immediate manual database checkpoint and WAL reset Interactive REPL ( whisk repl ) # Launching whisk without arguments (or with whisk repl ) enters the interactive REPL: ./build/debug/app/whisk REPL Prompt & Multi-Line Editing # Single statements ending in a semicolon ; execute immediately. Unfinished statements show a continuation prompt ( ...> ): whisk > CREATE TABLE inventory ( ... > item_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY , ... > name TEXT NOT NULL , ... > stock INTEGER DEFAULT 0 ... > ); Query OK , 0 rows affected ( round trip 0 . 39 ms ) Dot Commands # Inside the REPL, commands starting with a dot . control shell session operations: Dot Command Description .help Display the list of available REPL commands .ping Send a ping request and display round-trip latency .logs Print the recent server execution log buffer .snapshot Trigger a manual server checkpoint .quit , .exit Disconnect and terminate the REPL session Table Formatting # SELECT queries are automatically rendered into aligned ASCII tables: whisk > INSERT INTO inventory ( name , stock ) VALUES ( 'Espresso Beans' , 250 ), ( 'Oat Milk' , 40 ); Query OK , 2 rows affected , last_insert_rowid = 2 ( round trip 0 . 41 ms ) whisk > SELECT item_id , name , stock FROM inventory WHERE stock < 50 ; + ---------+----------+-------+ | item_id | name | stock | + ---------+----------+-------+ | 2 | Oat Milk | 40 | + ---------+----------+-------+ 1 row in set ( 0 . 32 ms ) Non-Interactive CLI Commands # Query Execution ( sql ) # Run SQL queries directly from automation scripts or shell pipelines: ./build/debug/app/whisk sql "SELECT COUNT(*) AS total_items FROM inventory;" Output: +-------------+ | total_items | +-------------+ | 2 | +-------------+ 1 row in set (0.28 ms) Server Health & Latency ( ping ) # Check server availability and network round-trip time: ./build/debug/app/whisk ping Output: PONG in 184 us Server Logs Inspection ( logs ) # Stream diagnostic server logs: ./build/debug/app/whisk logs Manual Checkpoint ( snapshot ) # Force an atomic snapshot and WAL truncation: ./build/debug/app/whisk snapshot Planned Whisk Module Commands Commands for managing server-side WebAssembly modules ( whisk init , whisk build , whisk test , whisk publish , and whisk call ) are part of the upcoming WASM engine release. See Development Status for milestone tracking. 3. C++ Client SDK ( WhiskClient ) # The C++ Client SDK provides a type-safe, zero-copy client interface for integrating WhiskDB directly into C++23 applications. Including the Header # Add include/ to your compiler search path and include the SDK header: #include "client/whisk_client.hpp" #include "client/table_format.hpp" Link your executable against whiskdb_core . API Reference: WhiskClient # namespace database { class WhiskClient { public : WhiskClient (); ~ WhiskClient (); // Prevent copying and moving (manages an active TCP connection) WhiskClient ( const WhiskClient & ) = delete ; WhiskClient & operator = ( const WhiskClient & ) = delete ; // Connection lifecycle Result < void > Connect ( const std :: string & host , uint16_t port ); void Close (); bool IsConnected () const ; // Server operations Result < uint64_t > Ping (); Result < QueryResult > Query ( std :: string_view sql , std :: span < const Value > params = {}); Result < std :: string > Snapshot (); Result < std :: string > GetLogs (); }; } // namespace database Method Details # Method Parameters Return Value Description Connect() const std::string& host , uint16_t port Result<void> Establishes a persistent TCP connection to the WhiskDB server Close() (none) void Closes the underlying socket connection IsConnected() (none) bool Returns true if the socket is currently connected Ping() (none) Result<uint64_t> Sends Opcode::Ping and returns round-trip duration in microseconds Query() std::string_view sql , std::span<const Value> params Result<QueryResult> Executes SQL statement(s), returning column headers and typed rows Snapshot() (none) Result<std::string> Requests the server to flush an atomic snapshot checkpoint GetLogs() (none) Result<std::string> Retrieves the engine execution logs from the server Data Model & Results # SQL Values ( Value ) # WhiskDB represents dynamically typed SQL values via std::variant : namespace database { using Blob = std :: vector < uint8_t > ; // 0: Null, 1: int64_t, 2: double, 3: std::string, 4: Blob using Value = std :: variant < std :: monostate , int64_t , double , std :: string , Blob > ; enum class ValueType : uint8_t { Null = 0 , Int64 = 1 , Double = 2 , Text = 3 , Blob = 4 }; } // namespace database Query Results ( QueryResult ) # namespace database { struct QueryResult { std :: vector < std :: string > columns ; // Column names (empty for non-SELECT DML) std :: vector < std :: vector < Value >> rows ; // Row-major cell matrix idx_t rows_affected = 0 ; // Number of rows modified (for INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE) int64_t last_insert_rowid = 0 ; // Auto-generated primary key from last insert uint64_t exec_us = 0 ; // Server-side execution time in microseconds bool is_mutation = false ; // True if statement modified database state }; } // namespace database Result Formatting Utilities # std::string FormatResultTable(const QueryResult& qr) : Renders an ASCII box-drawing table with column alignment, row counts, and execution metrics. std::vector<std::string> SplitStatements(std::string& buffer) : Splits multi-line SQL input into complete, semicolon-terminated statements while respecting quotes and escapes. Complete C++23 Integration Example # #include "client/whisk_client.hpp" #include "client/table_format.hpp" #include <iostream> #include <print> int main () { using namespace database ; WhiskClient client ; // 1. Connect to WhiskDB auto conn_res = client . Connect ( "127.0.0.1" , 8080 ); if ( ! conn_res ) { std :: println ( stderr , "Connection failed: {}" , conn_res . error (). Message ()); return 1 ; } std :: println ( "Connected to WhiskDB server." ); // 2. Measure latency with Ping auto ping_res = client . Ping (); if ( ping_res ) { std :: println ( "Ping latency: {} us" , * ping_res ); } // 3. Execute DDL schema creation auto ddl_res = client . Query ( "CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS accounts (" " id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, " " owner TEXT NOT NULL, " " balance REAL NOT NULL" ");" ); if ( ! ddl_res ) { std :: println ( stderr , "DDL error: {}" , ddl_res . error (). Message ()); return 1 ; } // 4. Insert data auto insert_res = client . Query ( "INSERT INTO accounts (owner, balance) VALUES ('Alice', 1250.75), ('Bob', 300.00);" ); if ( insert_res ) { std :: println ( "Inserted rows: {}, last rowid: {}" , insert_res -> rows_affected , insert_res -> last_insert_rowid ); } // 5. Query data and inspect typed rows auto query_res = client . Query ( "SELECT id, owner, balance FROM accounts ORDER BY id ASC;" ); if ( ! query_res ) { std :: println ( stderr , "Query error: {}" , query_res . error (). Message ()); return 1 ; } // Print formatted table using SDK utility std :: print ( "{}" , FormatResultTable ( * query_res )); // Access individual cells programmatically for ( idx_t row_idx = 0 ; row_idx < query_res -> rows . size (); ++ row_idx ) { const auto & row = query_res -> rows [ row_idx ]; int64_t id = std :: get < int64_t > ( row [ 0 ]); const std :: string & owner = std :: get < std :: string > ( row [ 1 ]); double balance = std :: get < double > ( row [ 2 ]); std :: println ( "Account #{}: {} (Balance: ${:.2f})" , id , owner , balance ); } // 6. Graceful disconnect client . Close (); return 0 ; } Error Handling Policy # The SDK uses the monadic Result<T> template rather than throwing C++ exceptions: - Success : Check if (result) or evaluate result.has_value() . Retrieve the value via *result or result.value() . - Failure : Extract the error details via result.error().Code() and result.error().Message() . Operational errors (network disconnections, SQL syntax errors, constraint violations) are always returned through Result<T> . Exceptions are reserved for unrecoverable host failures.
